page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 storage- and memory-oriented virtual machine operating on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 3839 GB of local SSD storage. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 5 Gbps, and there are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest per-thread capabilities offset by steady multi-core execution. The Intel Xeon 8163 architecture delivers lower-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 946.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 1103.88. Multi-core testing returns intermediate results across stress-ng (11742.55) and Geekbench multi-core (5855.0). Memory bandwidth reaches 66.14 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 58.29 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests show standard transactional and data throughput, achieving 11.7 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, 4310.67 in PassMark database operations, and 7.76 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.i2ne.4xlarge centers on its reliance on older generation CPU cores against its sizable local storage and memory footprint. While single-thread compression and medium-sized LLM processing perform in the bottom quarter of cloud tiers, the generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with 3.8 TB of fast local SSD creates strong cost-per-gigabyte utility for data-heavy platforms. This configuration fits relational and NoSQL databases, transactional caches, log aggregation nodes, and storage-intensive backend services that require substantial local capacity and memory headroom over raw single-threaded compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.4xlarge is a dedicated instance tailored for storage and memory-heavy operations. Driven by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, it provides 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) alongside 128.0 GB of system memory and 3839 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is rated at a 5 Gbps baseline. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate modest single-core throughput, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 946.0, but stable multi-threaded execution with a multi-core score of 5855.0 and 11.7 million Redis SET operations per second. While unsuited for single-threaded tasks or intensive machine learning inference, the large local disk allocation and 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provide practical density for relational databases, Redis caching layers, and search index nodes.
